To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a persuasive dialogue should be able to combine the current logic-based approach to persuasion with the novel emotional approach to persuasion; 2) a dialogue manager that implements the persuasive dialogue should have a model for the user that includes both the user’s beliefs, goals, and preferences as well as the user’s emotions, personality and social context; 3) a persuasive dialogue manager should be able to detect the user’s emotions and personality traits, as well as the social context; 4)
the following aspects of persuasion are necessary for health-care dialogue management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for a persuasive dialogue system, which is capable of producing efficient and effective persuasion in a health-care dialogue.
(1) how to model persuasion in a dialogue system; (2) which persuasive strategies are more effective; (3) how to implement the strategies; and (4) how to evaluate them.

the following questions: (i) how to use argumentation in a persuasive way, (ii) how to use emotional cues to render persuasion more effective, (iii) how to use a combination of logical and emotional cues for persuasion, (iv) how to use these techniques for health-care advising.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a persuasive dialogue is a dialogue that is both efficient in the sense of being able to persuade the user to take the desired action and comfortable in the sense that it does not annoy the user.
the future of human computer dialogue management will have to be based on persuasive argumentation and emotional cues.
the combination of the two approaches is the most promising for a persuasive dialogue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of persuasive argumentation is a promising field for future research.
the user should feel that the computer is a real interlocutor and is trying to help him or her.
we propose a new architecture for a health-care dialogue system, based on a new model of persuasion, and we show the feasibility of the model by a prototype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current logical approach is not enough to produce a comfortable persuasive dialogue.
the emotional cues are not only important to the success of the dialogue but also to the success of persuasion itself.
a persuasive agent should be able to adapt the way it communicates to the user's preferences and the situation.
